verdict.left_looks: A small, low house with red walls and a steep stepped dark-brown roof whose front is a stepped gable. Pale stone trim frames a large central opening with a checkered interior visible, sandstone corner pilasters carry square carved patterns, and a grey stone plinth runs along the base. The side has a row of small grey-framed windows. Clean and simple with little weathering. The roof reads as a single dark prism, and the front has a wooden fence-like railing.
verdict.right_looks: A larger barn-like building with a bold red body, white quoined corners, and a white stepped-crenellated gable. The roof is dark slate-grey with a cupola or chimney-like block on top. The front has a checkered red-and-white facade, a dark wooden canopy over the door, hanging lanterns, barrels, hay bales, and a fenced yard. The base is a cobblestone plinth on a grass-and-dirt island. The side walls are plain red with small windows, and the dark roof reads somewhat like a lid.
verdict.why: The right build has more character and presence from the canopy, lanterns, props, and full site base, while the left is a plainer house with a roof that reads as a single prism; craft is comparable, so the difference is mainly in detail and street presence.
